Senses.Explanation: The second half of the Layman Fu's inherited verse: without form, of itself still and empty. Langye Huijue raises the old sage's verse at the hall seat and faults it as a fine verse that falls in two pieces, offering the single eye to whoever can check it out, Jinian Jingxian presses the old saying half by half at the winter-solstice small meeting, then lifts the staff, strikes once, and answers with his own red-bare verse, Wuyi Yuanlai raises it in the collected-essentials record, rules the old saying a lone walk that holds everything forth, and seconds Zhu Xi's admission that his own school has no such words, and Tianyin Yuanxiu tells the year-end assembly that after forty years of probing the affair is still just so, recites the verse, shouts, and calls even it rambling talk, sending them all back for tea. Zhuanyu Guanheng writes the half for a lay patron as the good hiding, since by hiding well it can master and never rest, backing the reading with the Ode and the Document, Minshu Ruxiang lifts the staff on the first half, drops it on the shapeless half, lifts it again on the lower lines, and asks where the master of the ten-thousand forms settles, Gusu Zun recites the verse and holds that to meet it before words is to know where one's own root star of life stands, and so where the old teachers' stands, and Baiyu Jingsi interrogates the verse line by line at the eighty-year birthday seat, draws a circle for the shapeless half, and faults the ancients' talk as a Hangzhou boatman's patter.
